questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to go to Italy and found many relevant courses at University of Milan.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, it has been an amazing experience! Although there has been some complications in the beginning of the stay due to an unfixed course calendar.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quit easy. But instead of receiving one mail containing all the information needed, I received several, which I believe could have been done differently.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not really any. There was ESN but that was really uncoordinated.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was really lucky. My mother knew someone who had an apartment.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It might be difficult to find a place and quit expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to choose courses and see if it was possible to have all courses in the same sceduale. But you first recieved the tool for doing so after arrival. You had to register for the courses a long time after arrival, which was great since you could decide after having the course. However, all in all the registration process was very confusing.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I wrote the Erasmus-responsible many emails, otherwise there was not much help available.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I only ended up having 2/5 of the courses that i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: dont bother which courses you choose when aplaying for Erasmus in the first place - wait until you have the tool to see which courses are possible to have without them overlapping.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Compared to the fact that the courses was MA courses, I think the level was very low. The expectations of the students was very low and the read burden was very little.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Only lectures at the University of Milan, compared to more variated forms e.g. group work

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Gender Justice 
Environmental and Food Law 
Private Public Partnership for Sustainable Development 
Women in Tech: New Frontiers of Gender-Related Rights and Artificial Intelligence
Society, Law and Development

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can really recommend 'Environmental and Food Law'! The teachers were very compitent and this was the only course with variated teaching style.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I bought a used bicycle for €70

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Compared to Denmark, It was very inexpensive to go out to eat, which I enjoyed a lot.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found it dificuelt to find a football club and I also missed a "friday-bar" at the campus as we have at UCPH.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not much. There was a women's football teams, but that was far out of town and only 5pers.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to go out of the city by train, e.g. Lago de Como, it only costs €5.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend to go to Firenze, you can go by bus which is very cheap compared to the trains. You can also go to the dolomites, I went with a couple of friends and rented a car and a little cottage - its so beautiful

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took my a couple of weeks to get used to the nongelan Italian approach to everything - both in trafic, school and everywhere else.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take them for an Aperol Spritz outside campus and an aperativo after class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The noglelan approach in all areas - both at the university, in trafic and everywhere else. Also its quit conservative compared to Copenhagen.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Although it was one of the things I found most challenging with the culture, I also found the noglelan approach very relaxing.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go out of town, e.g. to Lago de Como or Crema by train - it only costs €5. 

Don't buy a bicycle - the traffic is insane. 

Enjoy the many good restaurants e.g. Serafina (my personal favorite) and the museums.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient with the system - everything might seem very frustrating, but it will all turn out fine in the end.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It found it very nice to be without any obligations for a while - no job, no family and friends etc. I have a felling that I've been on vacation for a half year.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having patience with the system and not stress about it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
